replies.author: @kyleoates6367
replies.text:
Because to keep the lights on, the insane rents paid (this isn't just a private issue, but also a commercial one right now), insurance paid in case you get sued, and shop properly stocked you need to take $60, not $30. So after paying $30/hr to the mechanic... you're left with -$10. So you have to charge $90/hr to break even at a rate the mechanic isn't happy with. Aaaaaaand then you have to pay yourself and any other non-mechanic employees you might have. So now you're charging $120 so you can pay the mechanic $40/hr, $60 to break even with overhead and liability costs, and $20 to yourself to handle the non-mechanic needs and some mechanic needs as well of the company. But since you don't want to make less than your employee, you charge $150/hr so you're making $50/hr and they're making $40/hr. But here's the thing, there's no wiggle room. Prices shoot up 10% because some orange idiot in the white house puts a blanket tariff on things and now you're screweed.

It's different if you're the only person doing it, but then you're doing EVERYTHING and you can't take more repair jobs and increase profits that way. You'll be busy, but not profitable. And you still run the risk of some idiot in the white house playing with the entire world's economy like it's their personal piggy bank.

comments.text:
When I was working at a dealership, they would charge $123 for one hour diagnostic. Out of that I only got $16. Some will go to the advisor and the rest is to the dealership. When you are flat rate, you will push yourself to sickness to try to make 40 hours a week. What will hold you back is not having the parts, customers taking a long time to get back to you and advisors not selling.

The main reason I left is when my boss told me that I had to "kick it into the next gear." What next gear? I cant put anything to the customers head and force them to buy something, they do not want to. I just work on the car, tell them what they need, and the advisor sells.

The problem is that the cars have so much tech in them, that its more work. But the shop owner refuse to pay more due to what it take to work on the car. So pay more or remove all that tech, make more room and have it that we can get the job done at the speed of warranty. Plus, we will have more customer pay work.
